 Anyone who has spent a few winters in west Pasco knows the routine. You run to the store on Little Road, then head to a doctor visit off US 19 near Ridge Road. By mid-morning, State Road 54 is backed up, and snowbird season only adds more cars. A fender bender in a plaza lot is a nuisance. A real crash can mean a broken hip, months of therapy and a stack of forms.
 Picking a lawyer is not the time to grab the first name off a billboard. You want someone nearby, easy to reach and patient enough to explain each step. Florida drivers carry PIP coverage, which generally pays part of your medical bills and lost pay no matter who caused the crash. Each firm below keeps an office in New Port Richey.

 1. Roman Austin – A Seven Springs Office Close to Trinity and Holiday 
 Type: Personal injury law firm
 Focus: Car crash injuries, plus truck, motorcycle, pedestrian and rideshare claims
 Location: Seven Springs Boulevard, New Port Richey
 Roman Austin’s Pasco County office sits on Seven Springs Boulevard, close to Trinity. The team serves New Port Richey, Port Richey, Holiday, Hudson and Trinity, along with parts of north Pinellas. Folks hurt at a spot like US 19 and Main Street can sit down with a New Port Richey car accident lawyer without a long drive into Tampa or Clearwater.
 Founder Mark S. Roman is Board Certified in civil trial law by The Florida Bar, an honor that fewer than 2 in 100 Florida lawyers hold. He also has an AV rating from Martindale-Hubbell and a place on The National Trial Lawyers Top 100.
 Partner John C. Austin has been named to Super Lawyers and Best Lawyers. Partner Miles H. Hickman, an Eagle Scout, made the Best Lawyers: Ones to Watch list. The firm takes cases on a contingency fee and says you pay no attorney fee unless a recovery is made for you. Its phones are answered around the clock, and the first meeting costs nothing.
 Roman Austin Car Accident and Personal Injury Lawyers, 2515 Seven Springs Blvd, New Port Richey, FL 34655 | (727) 787-2500 | romanaustin.com
 2. KFB Law – A Cita Lane Office in the Mill Pond Professional Center 
 Type: Personal injury law firm
 Focus: Car, motorcycle, truck and pedestrian accident claims
 Location: Cita Lane, New Port Richey
 Kinney, Fernandez & Boire, P.A., known as KFB Law, has a New Port Richey office on Cita Lane in the Mill Pond Professional Center. The firm also has offices around Tampa Bay. Its team speaks Spanish, Hindi and Vietnamese, which can help families who prefer another language. The firm says it will meet clients at home or in the hospital.
 KFB Law, 7617 Cita Lane, Suite 102, New Port Richey, FL 34653 | (727) 846-1680 | kfblaw.com
 3. Wendy Doyle-Palumbo, PA – A Missouri Avenue Practice With Public Service Roots 
 Type: Personal injury and family law practice
 Focus: Car, motorcycle and truck crash claims, plus PIP disputes
 Location: Missouri Avenue, New Port Richey
 Wendy Doyle-Palumbo started her career as a paralegal. She later served as an Assistant Attorney General and a Guardian Ad Litem attorney before opening her own practice. Her New Port Richey office is on Missouri Avenue, and she keeps a second office in Hudson. Her firm also has a family law side.
 Wendy Doyle-Palumbo, PA, 5727 Missouri Ave, Suite 211, New Port Richey, FL 34652 | (727) 263-3319 | injuryattorneypascofl.com 
 4. Denmon Pearlman Law – A Downtown Main Street Injury Practice 
 Type: Personal injury law firm
 Focus: Accident and injury claims
 Location: Main Street, downtown New Port Richey
 Denmon Pearlman Law is an injury firm with an office on Main Street in the heart of the city. Attorney Christian M. Denmon is listed at this location. The firm handles accident and injury claims for people hurt on Pasco County roads.
 Denmon Pearlman Law, 5703 Main St, New Port Richey, FL 34652 | (727) 753-0049 | denmonpearlman.com
 How a Seasoned Crash Lawyer Earns Their Keep 
 A lawyer who handles car crash claims every day knows things a generalist may not. They know how to make sense of a police report, which records an adjuster will ask for and how to find a second insurance policy. They also know when an offer is fair and when it falls short.
 That matters a great deal for older drivers. Insurers sometimes blame a sore back or a bad hip on age instead of the crash. A seasoned injury lawyer knows how to show what changed after the wreck, using your medical history and the people who see you every day.
 A Final Word for Pasco County Drivers 
 New Port Richey has several solid choices for car accident help, and each firm here has a local door you can walk through. Even so, Roman Austin stands out from the pack. Its office on Seven Springs Boulevard is close to home for much of west Pasco. Its founder’s Florida Bar certification as a civil trial lawyer is a mark few in the state ever reach. The partners bring honors of their own, and someone picks up the phone at any hour. If a crash on US 19, Little Road or State Road 54 has left you hurting, see a doctor first. Keep every bill, and jot down the names of anyone who saw the wreck. Then call a New Port Richey car accident lawyer you can trust. For many readers, that call will go to Roman Austin.
